title: Calculate a factorial
description: Write a function `factorial(n)` that returns `n!` (the product of every integer from 1 to `n`). `factorial(0)` is `1`.
hints: Idea to consider: an accumulator that multiplies, the same shape as a summing loop but with * instead of +
Starting a running total at 1 (not 0 - multiplying by 0 would zero everything out) and multiplying it by each number from 1 to n builds up the factorial one step at a time.
Loop i from 1 to n inclusive, multiplying an accumulator starting at 1 by i each time, and return the accumulator.
explanation: The accumulator starts at 1 (the multiplicative identity) rather than 0, since multiplying anything by 0 would collapse the whole product to 0 on the very first step.
